ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The asymptotic Bode magnitude curve in the figure has angular frequency ω as the horizontal axis and magnitude(dB) as the vertical axis. The low-frequency segment is an upward straight line, with the slope marked as 20 dB/dec, and it passes through 0 dB at ω=0.5. Then the curve becomes a horizontal plateau, with the plateau magnitude marked as 12 dB. The high-frequency segment descends from the plateau as a broken line downward, with the slope marked as -40 dB/dec, and it passes through 0 dB at ω=8. Reasoning: The initial slope is +20 dB/dec, indicating that there is one zero at the origin, so first write it as G(s)=Ks/(...). The rising asymptote is 0 dB when ω=0.5, so |Kjω|=1; substituting ω=0.5 gives K=2. The rising line rises from 0 dB at ω=0.5 to the 12 dB plateau, and the frequency ratio is 10^(12/20), so the first break frequency is 0.5×10^(12/20)≈2 rad/s. Here the slope changes from +20 dB/dec to 0, indicating that there is one pole at ω=2, corresponding to the factor 1+s/2=1+0.5s. The high-frequency segment changes from a horizontal plateau to -40 dB/dec, indicating that there are two coincident poles at the second break point. This descending line reaches ω=8 when it drops from 12 dB to 0 dB, with slope -40 dB/dec, so the second break frequency is 8/10^(12/40)≈4 rad/s, corresponding to the repeated pole factor (1+s/4)^2=(1+0.25s)^2. Combining gives the transfer function G(s)=2s/[(1+0.5s)(1+0.25s)^2].

method.method_draft: From the initial +20 dB/dec slope, infer one zero at the origin, so start with G(s)=K s/(...). Since the rising asymptote crosses 0 dB at omega=0.5, use |Kjomega|=1 at omega=0.5 to get K=2. The line rises from 0 dB at 0.5 to the 12 dB plateau, so the first break is at omega=0.5*10^(12/20)≈2; the slope changes from +20 to 0, indicating one pole at omega=2, giving factor 1+s/2=1+0.5s. The final slope is -40 dB/dec from a flat slope, so there must be two coincident poles at the second break. Since a -40 dB/dec line drops 12 dB before reaching 0 dB at omega=8, the break is omega=8/10^(12/40)≈4, giving repeated factor (1+s/4)^2=(1+0.25s)^2. Combine these as G(s)=2s/[(1+0.5s)(1+0.25s)^2].
